takeaway: Tibial nerve: roots L4 to S3, deep to soleus in the calf, divides into medial and lateral plantar nerves in the foot; in the popliteal fossa it gives a cutaneous branch, the sural nerve.

question.text: Which of the following statements regarding the tibial nerve is correct?

answer.text: Cutaneous supply within the popliteal fossa is via a branch of the sural nerve.

lines.text: The tibial nerve starts from the roots L4, L5, S1, S2 and S3.
It crosses the popliteal fossa, then runs down the calf deep to soleus, not superficial to it.
At the ankle it ends by dividing into the medial and lateral plantar nerves, in the foot.
In the popliteal fossa it gives muscle branches to gastrocnemius, popliteus and soleus, so it does supply extrinsic muscles.
It also gives a cutaneous branch there: the sural nerve, carrying skin sensation.
So the correct statement is the cutaneous supply through a branch of the sural nerve.
